subject: Hindi
text: Surdas (1478-1583) was a great poet of the Krishna Bhakti movement who composed in Braj Bhasha. His major work is Sursagar. First pad: describes baby Krishna taking his first steps; Mother Yashoda lovingly supports him. Second pad: Gopiyon ka Viyog (grief of the Gopis). After Krishna leaves for Mathura, Uddhav arrives with message of Yoga (path of knowledge). Gopis refuse saying their hearts are fixed on Krishna - the famous 'Uddhav mana na bhaye das bees' line. Uddhav is compared to a lotus leaf (untouched by water). Main themes: devotion (bhakti), separation (viyog shringar), and surrender to God.

subject: Hindi
text: Tulsidas (1532-1623) composed Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi language. This excerpt is from Balkand: after Ram breaks Shiva's bow, Parshuram arrives furious. Lakshman engages in witty and bold debate. Ram remains calm and humble saying there is no fault of mine. Three contrasting characters: Parshuram's arrogance and anger, Ram's humility and composure, Lakshman's bold and sarcastic responses. Language is Awadhi. Ras (emotional sentiment): Veer (heroic) and Hasya (comic). Alankar (figures of speech): Anupras (alliteration), Upma (simile). Lesson: humility overcomes arrogance; one should remain calm even when provoked.

subject: Hindi
text: Dev (1673-1767) was a major Riti period poet. Riti period features: abundance of Shringar ras (romance), display of literary devices (alankar), use of Braj Bhasha. Savaiya: describes Krishna beauty - his red face, dark curly hair, beautiful eyes - his beauty surpasses even Kamdev (god of love). Kavitt: beautiful description of spring season (Basant) awakening love and emotion in nature. Themes: beauty of Krishna, beauty of nature, Shringar ras. The Savaiya and Kavitt are specific poetic meters. Dev excels in describing physical beauty using rich imagery and metaphor in Braj language.

subject: Hindi
text: Jaishankar Prasad (1889-1937) was one of the four pillars of Chhayavad poetry (Prasad, Pant, Nirala, Mahadevi Verma). In Aatmakathya (self-narrative), the poet says he does not want to write his autobiography as it would only be a record of sorrows that would pain others. His life had little joy and much grief. He says what is the use of narrating a life filled only with sorrow? Even his moments of love remained incomplete and unfulfilled. Themes: pain (vedana), sadness (vishad), self-reflection. Artistic qualities: symbolism, emotional depth. The poem is notable for its refusal to write autobiography - an ironic self-biography.

subject: Hindi
chapter: Kshitij: Nirala - Utsah aur At Nahin Rahi Hai
text: Suryakant Tripathi Nirala (1896-1961) was a Chhayavad poet known for independence and rebellion. Utsah: Nirala calls upon clouds (badal) to come thundering and raining. The cloud is not just a rain-bringer but a symbol of revolution and social transformation - bringing new consciousness to society. At Nahin Rahi Hai: describes the overwhelming beauty of the month of Phalgun (spring). Nature is so beautiful it cannot be contained in anything - it overflows everywhere. Mahua flowers blooming, leaves turning green, nature rejoicing. Nirala poetry shows enthusiasm (utsah), rebellion, love of nature, and deep human sensitivity.

subject: Hindi
chapter: Kshitij: Nagarjun - Yeh Danturit Muskan aur Fasal
text: Nagarjun (1911-1998) was a progressive peoples poet. Yeh Danturit Muskan: the poet sees a baby smile with new teeth; even a stone would melt and death would gain life from this innocent smile. This smile represents the power and vitality of life itself. Fasal (Crop): the crop is not just the farmers labor but the combined result of rivers water, mountain soil, the work of millions of hands, and the warmth of the sun. The crop symbolises the importance of human labor and cooperation with nature. Themes: joy of childhood, value of human labor, dignity of farmers, harmony between human beings and nature.

subject: Hindi
text: Mangalesh Dabral (1948-2020) was a contemporary poet concerned with social suffering. Sangatkar (accompanist): describes the supporting singer who accompanies the main vocalist. When the main singer reaches high notes, the accompanist quietly follows at a lower pitch - his voice sometimes trembles. The accompanist deliberately keeps his voice below the main singer - this is not his weakness but his humanity. He does not want to let the main artist falter or fail. Theme: the importance of support and sacrifice; those who remain anonymous yet make crucial contributions deserve recognition; in life, many people quietly support others and enable their success.

subject: Hindi
text: This story is set in a small town. The municipality installed a statue of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose without glasses. Captain the eyeglass seller would always place a real pair of glasses on the statue - changing them when customers bought those frames. Captain is old, poor, and helpless but his patriotism is unshakeable. One day Captain dies. Later, a child places glasses made from reed grass on the statue. This symbolises that the feeling of patriotism lives on in the hearts of ordinary people. Theme: true patriotism, the feelings of common people, symbolism, patriotism does not need grand gestures but sincere sentiment.

subject: Hindi
text: Ramvriksh Benipuri wrote this in the Rekha-chitra (character sketch) form. Balgobin Bhagat is an unusual character - a householder living like a saint. He follows only Sahib (Kabir). He sings devotional songs even while working in the fields. He does not allow anyone in his house to lie or misbehave. When his son dies, he stops his daughter-in-law from crying - he says it is the soul liberation. After his son death he sings and dances in Kartik month. He wants to arrange his daughter-in-law remarriage - a progressive thought. One day he dies while singing kirtan. Theme: devotion and renunciation, uniqueness of character, balance between worldly life and spirituality.

subject: Hindi
text: Yashpal satirical story. The narrator boards a train. A nawab (nobleman) is sitting alone and is annoyed at the narrator presence. The nawab carefully prepares a cucumber - peels it, cuts it, adds salt - then smells it and throws it out of the window. The narrator is astonished. Nawab says the cucumber is delicate in nature (nazuk tabiyat). This is the satirical point: the nawab pretentious aristocratic style and show of refinement. He cannot actually enjoy the cucumber but must maintain his image of refinement. Theme: artificial pride, pretentious behaviour, satirical portrayal of feudal mentality and its absurd display of status.

subject: Hindi
text: This autobiographical narrative depicts childhood of Bholanath (the author). Bholanath spends much time with his father - going to the river bank at dawn, sitting in puja, riding on his father shoulders. But whenever there is any fear or trouble, the child immediately runs to his mother lap. When frightened by a snake he leaves his father and runs to his mother. The mother aanchal (the loose end of her saree) is the safest place in the world. Theme: the incomparable love and protection of a mother, the innocence of childhood, village environment, both parents importance but mother is the ultimate refuge.

subject: Hindi
text: Kamleshwar satirical story. A statue of King George V (British king) in Delhi has a broken nose. Before Queen Elizabeth visit, there is chaos to fix it. The sculptor searches all over India measuring noses of statues of great men but finds no suitable nose. Finally it is suggested to cut the nose of a living Indian. Someone nose is cut and put on the statue. The satire: to honour the remnants of British rule the Indian dignity (naak literally means nose but also means honor) is sacrificed. Theme: criticism of colonial mentality that persists after independence, the irony of honoring colonial monuments while sacrificing Indian dignity.

subject: Hindi
chapter: Kritika: Sana Sana Haath Jodi (Madhu Kankaria)
text: Madhu Kankaria travel narrative. The author travels to Sikkim and Gangtok. She meets a little girl saying morning prayers with joined hands (sana sana haath jodi means small small hands folded in prayer). Extraordinary natural beauty: snow-covered mountains, waterfalls, colourful flowers. The lives of army soldiers in difficult conditions protecting the country. Katao described as India Switzerland. The simple and peaceful lives of local people living in nature. Theme: conservation of environment, natural beauty, importance of simple living, value of travel and experiencing different cultures, gratitude for natural gifts.
